# Chapter Fourteen: Forced Choices

Forced in Either

Corliss climed upon the large brown horse and slid the Silvan Repeating rifle into the saddle holster, as she moved, she noticed the larger barrel revolvers that had replaced her muskets rubbing against her legs. She was going to need to adjust those she thought smiling. The weapons looked amazing and she couldn’t wait to test fire them she thought. Dara finally made it up onto her horse and the two set out from the stables.

Based on the directions the soldier had given Marcus it would take them three days to reach the Tower and most of that will be in woods she reflected wanting to steer clear of any roads that Soldiers might be using to move supplies. Dara stayed close behind mimicking her movements and Corliss nodded in approval. Before she could get too far a bellowing voice came from behind and Corliss stopped turning on her horse as she smiled. Uri came rushing up to stand next to her horse. “Be Careful, we don’t know what the Empress has been up to, in that place” he said and Corliss patted his check gently in a very daughter like fashion “Ill be fine, you however better be here when I get back” she said and didn’t do a very good job hiding the worry in her voice. He smiled and squeezed her hand. “I will” he said gruffly and turned, heading back to the stables Corliss watched as he rubbed at his eyes and smiled. Who did he think he was fooling she thought, nudging her horse forward as the set out west?

“So, whats are plan?” Dara asked as she move up to ride next to the Warden, the woods where tight but she managed to maintain the position despite having to move around trees and other detritus Corliss nodded in approval at the Mages horsemanship.

“We show up, kill a bunch of bad guys, save Maelen, have lunch” she said smiling as Dara eyed her partner for this mission, the concern on her face was almost overwhelming “Please tell me we have a better plan then that” she said and still smiling Corliss pulled ahead pushing her horse faster towards there goal. Corliss thought about the question and she would love nothing more then to put the Mage’s mind at east but she honestly didn’t have a plan and the only reason she had agreed to this was the mage was needed at the city, without him she was positive her people would be expelled and show needed to ensure her people were safe, besides she owed the fucking Empress for taking the keep and Corliss was determined to break of a piece of that woman’s ass. If Maelen was important then it was time to play take away she thought smiling.

The rode for the rest of the day, the lush forest there shelter as they parralelled roads, one twice was they forced to stop as patrols laden with carts of supplies passed by, the soldiers distracted as they rode on chatting about the coming battle. Corliss narrowed her eyes both times, weighing the thought of taking the band of the Empresss protectorate in their exuberance at killing her friends. Corliss swallowed the thought; she did not need to advertise a trail as to where they were headed. Until recently according to the soldier the Tower had been the Empress’s best kept secret, now that the Chosen and her Screamers were public knowledge she no longer needed to hide it, in fact to hear the soldier tell it, the woman was practically gushing at the progress they were making in ‘perfecting mages’ Corliss had seen the screamers, if that was perfecting mages she shuddered to think what the woman was cooking up next.

That morning the two had stopped at Corliss’s request, as the horses were set to pasture as the Warden gathered the bag of resin cartidges and headed for the open field. Dara followed behind curious as Corliss began picking up pieces of fallen wood and setting them up. Taking forty paces she holstered the gun, then taking a breath she drew and shooting from this hip hit one of four targers.

Cursing she moved around shaking out her hands as she repeated Uri’s shoot mantra to herself “feet evenly apart, gun held comfortably, don’t hold it too tight, aim with both eyes, breath and squeeze” she said over and over. “What are you doing?” Dara finally asked as she watched this scene play out in front of her. “Getting use to the pistols, I will be no good until I am comfortable shooting these” she answered and Dara nodded, she could understand that these new guns were entirely different then the muskets and any new sword or staff always required time to settle in with it, understand the balance and the weight, so it must me like that she thought, watching as Corliss set up again and, again hit one of four targets. The Warden did this, over and over all morning as Dara watched. By the time she gathered the bag of cartidges even with all the shooting it had barely put a dent in it. Corliss could hit every target consistently. Mounting the horses, the two women set out again, riding west as the sun hung high in the sky. The Warden now felt more comfortable with the new guns, six shots per pistol, compared to the single shot weapons that she had become used to, was a game changer she reflected smiling as they rode on.

As mid-day began to descend into dusk, they came close to a village, Corliss stopped motioning for Dara to do the same “Whats wrong?” the mage asked hunkering down on the horse to lean in towards the Warden. Corliss shot her a slightly annoyed look and with the Mage looking suitably chastised the Warden focused on the village, something about it had rang an alarm in her head. She carefully surveyed the ghost town that was the town center as she tried to see as much as she could through the large open gates of the little village.

From the angle Corliss was viewing the small courtyard of the village the entire square looked empty, it wasn’t until she shifted left getting a better look at the front of the market buildings nestled on the left, then she stopped her blood running cold as she counted twenty people lined up and on there knees as a soldier in a dress uniform paced up and down the line.

Corliss wasn’t quite sure what was going on, but she knew a firing squad when she saw one and the line of soldiers behind the Officer looked very much like one. Anger flashed in her as she continued to watch the officer, his face smug as he continued to leisurly pace in front of the terrified residents on there knees. “Dara” the Warden whispered getting off of her horse. Even though she looked calm and collected inside her emotions were waging an internal battle, looking at the line of people she could see young and old, women and children all scared, some crying.

Corliss had given her oath to protect the people of Vicor, but by doing that could reveal her location and bring more soldiers down into the area, thus causing their mission to become next to impossible. Dara, crouching and moving carefully came over to stand next to her and looking over at the village, she too spotted the kneeling residents. The Mage’s simple comment sealed it for Corliss, there was no question, no conflict she just said “So, how are we getting them out?” and the Warden turned and smiled at her. “As quickly as possible” she answered and motioned for the mage to follow. The new spring growth of underbrush covered there approach to the fence as Corliss watched the soldiers, willing them to not look in there direction as they loaded and set the single shot rifles, everyone of them looking bored, there was no reservation or conflict in any of them as they stood there as if this was just another chore to be completed so they could get on with there day and that above all else sealed there fate.

Corliss waited and when she was sure they weren’t watching she and Dara bolted across the small open area, coming to the fence they knelt down, the mage closing her eyes and preparing herself as Corliss pulled the long elegant pistol and ensured it was loaded. The blue crystal resin cartridges showing in the cylinder, confirming six shots, she reholstered it and pulled the repeating rifle the long wooden stock smooth as she ran her hand over it coming to the metal of the side loading portal, she cocked the rifle, ejecting one of the cartridges, then reloaded it, checking to ensure it was full. Sixteen in the rifle and six in each pistol against the officer and twelve soldiers she thought.

Corliss closed her eyes and took a breath; now she had to hope that the time spent with the pistols would be enough and closing her eyes she took a breath. Turning to Dara she leaned in close “Anything you can do to ensure they don’t shoot back for a moment?” Corliss asked and the other woman smiled and simply nodded. Corliss and Dara edged closer to the entrance as they progressed they could hear the voice of the officer as he continued to drone one, by the time they stood next to the opening his voice was clear “Your performance has been incredibly disappointing, in fact it has been so bad, the Empress has ordered us to remove the bottom ten percent of workers because it is costing more to feed and house them then the work output they produce, you have disappointed the Empress, you have disappointed me and for that your only use is as fertilizer and examples to your fellow workers” he announced. Corliss turned and nodded at Dara. The mage closed her eyes, taking a breath as she gathered power to her, opening her eyes again Corliss could see the flash of blue as she stepped around the corner and with a flourish of her hand a bright light exploded in the middle of the group.

That was the only urging Corliss needed as she spun, coming around Dara and raising the rifle. She expelled her breath as the barrel came level with here eye, tucking the butt of the rifle into her shoulder she lined the metal bar on the end of the barrel onto the first soldier squeezing the trigger the gun recoiled, but surprising less then that of the single shot, she cracked the level, readjusting the gun and firing, she repeated this fourteen times, two of them misses as she spit a curse and fired a second shot. The soldiers dropped one after another as blue lines of energy followed the resin cartridge to explode in their chest.

Corliss glanced at the officer who had recovered from the bright light and was pulling his pistol. Corliss pulled hers first cocking back the hammer as she raised it and cracking off a hip shot it took the officer high in the shoulder spinning him. She cocked the hammer again and squeezed the trigger, this one hit the officer dead center as he rotated back towards the two women. He fell backward a loud grunt emitting from his mouth. Corliss panned the pistol over the courtyard seeking out threats and finding none. She quickly holstered it as the line of workers recovered from the bright light only to find there agressors dead on the ground. They began to get up, eyes wide with hope as they looked around a few shied away from Corliss as she pointed the gun at the ground and made a calming gesture with her hand. “I am not here to hurt you, but you need to move quickly, if there any soldiers in the vicinity they would have heard those shots” she said and led the group with her in the lead and Dara taking the rear as the line of people made their way back to the woods. Corliss stood by the edge of the overgrowth that started near the treeline and watching for anyone approaching as the group shambled into the woods, most still in shock as only a moment ago they were as good as dead.

Now, now they were alive and possibly free, she could see the smiles and the worry, and the fear and the hope mixed in all their faces as they walked by her. Once the last one disappeared and Dara right after them Corliss took one more look around and with a nod followed the group, they gathered sitting on fallen trees or the ground, most still in shock but some laughing and others smiling as the realization of their own mortality and how close they had come to meeting there maker hit them. Corliss allowed them some time to process, to relax and mostly to put some distance from what the worse experience of there life would possibly be.

After a time, she gathered everyone up, the two women ushering the group further north putting a half a day’s distance between the village and themselves before they truly aloud them to relax.

Once they had gotten settled the Warden left the group in Dara’s capable hands, going deeper into the woods Corliss spent the evening hunting, almost am hour later a deer thrown over her shoulder.

Hanging it from a tree far from the group, she bled and skinned it, the process and tasks of something well known to her, relaxing in its attention to detail. Once she had butchered the meat off of the carcass, Corliss returned to the camp to find Dara had already started a fire and began to gather sticks alloing them to stick the meat and cook it. The smell of an open fire and sizzling meat drew everyone as they all moved closer to the fire, everyone whispering to each other as they waited for the food to finish cooking.

“What are we going to do with these people” Dara whispered coming over to stand with Corliss as she stood on the edge of the camp watching the survivors and smiling herself, they had done good today, these people would live and she had stopped a massacre, despite what it mean might for tomorrow, today was a win and she would enjoy it. “Well we can’t take them with us” she said still reguarding the group of workers. “We have to send them somewhere; they surely can’t stay here” Corliss continued trying to think where they would be the safest.

They both thought about it in silence as they watched a man take charge, pulling meat from the fire and handing it out, children first, then women and then finally men. Once everyone was fed the man took the last and smallest piece for himself and Corliss nodded in approval. It wasn’t often you find someone worthy of leading, but when you did it was a nice reaffirmation of man in general, especially when you thought of the travestiest that were commited daily by the Empress and her new court. Corliss thought about it for a while, trying to figure out what to do with the group, they couldn’t just leave them, they were unarmed and not a soldier or mercenary among them she thought. However, they had a mission and one they had to complete and couldn’t bring these people along. It was quite a conundrum she found herself in.

Finally, she came to a compromise, motioning for Dara to join her, they walked a little way from the camp. “We are going to keep going west, but also North hopefully we can find some scouts who can take them otherwise we will pass within a day walk of the old Warden’s complex where the Messenger took the refugees” she finished, and Dara’s eyes went wide. “Wait, weren’t they attacked, what makes you think they will be safe there” she finished and Corliss winced a little and looked over at the group as they settled in, most resting, others unable to “Most lived and they haven’t been attacked since, besides there isn’t anywhere else they can go” Corliss finished and Dara was forced to agree.

The group settled in for the night, Corliss taking watch, she felt responsible for the workers now and knowing she wouldn’t forgive herself if anything happened to them. The Warden was awake the entire night, not trusting the watch to anyone else. The group began to move and wake about an hour before dawn, Corliss had already started a new fire and picking up her gear set out again to feed the workers before the day of walking they would have. Corliss spent an hour canvasing for worthy game when her luck changed and she happened upon a farm, it didn’t look lived in but it had been recently.

Checking over the pen she smiled as she noticed the flock of chickens still roaming in the fenced area. She returned like the victorious hero, twenty-eight chicken’s dead and hanging from strings over her back accompanied her. Setting them down, she found four people who began to dress the birds, preparing them for cooking. It took nearly two hours for the group to finish eating, clean up and prepare for the day’s journey Corliss was not happy with the time wasted but the Warden understood that most people didn’t spend a lot of time in the woods, even those who spent there lives on farms. They marched through the woods, Corliss using the sun to navigate them west and north and had been pleased with the time they were making when she began to hear familiar sounds echoing through the woods from just ahead. “Everyone down” Corliss hissed and watched as the happy faces turned alarmed and began to crouch down.

Dara made her way over to the Warden, keeping an eye out as she too heard the odd sounds. “Whats going on?” she asked still trying to get a look at whatever it was making the random beats against the ground. “Horses are feeding in a field close by, probably just beyond those bushes up there, if there are horses, there are probably soldiers” she finished and motioned for Dara to stay.

Corliss began to inch her way forward, deliberately moving branches so they wouldn’t break and rolling her feet instead of stepping straight down to minimize the rustling her walking would make. It took patience and control, but she finally made it to a place where she peaked through the thick brush and found herself staring into the face of a horse directly in front of her. The best looked at her and rose its head, nuzzling her hair and then going back to enjoying the grass. Corliss peaked around the animal and noticed soldiers, twenty at least sitting around and resting after a hard march.

She looked them over and then cocked her head, these were not the Empress’s soldiers, she noticed the symbols on the tunics, the all-seeing eye of the Knights of Aurtus. With a sigh of relief, she emerged from the brush, ensuring her weapons were holstered he called out to the group, startled they came to their feet, most reaching for weapons but when they saw her, weapons holstered and hands up most relaxed.

A few walked pasts her, looking to see if others were lying in wait and she had to appreciate that she thought because that would be the exact thing she would be doing in their shoes. “Who are you and what are you doing here” an older soldier with captains bars barked at her, eyeing her weapons suspiciously Corliss smiled trying to show a relaxed posture “I am Warden Corliss Bor, I am on a mission, but have come across refugees and was escorting them to the Warden Complex to the west of here” she said and watched as the captain visibly relaxed. “We received a request from the new Lord Reagent for aid, we are on our way there now” he stated, and Corliss smiled at her good fortune.

An hour later Dara and Corliss waved goodbye as the group moved onward under the escort of the Aurtus Knights “Well looks like we are back in mission” Dara said smiling at the workers as they moved off. “We are, and no time like the present” she laughed, walking over to the horses they had walked for the past two days and climed upon them. They had time to make up and a mission to complete. Urging the horse forward Corliss galloped off with Dara in her wake doing her best to keep up.

That night they rested in a clearing well out of sight of any roads and Corliss laid her back upon a tree as she watched the horses lazily eating the grass as the sun continued to descend behind the trees.

“What has happened to our world Corliss, I mean when did it become okay to treat people like cattle, slaughter them when they were no longer useful, basically when did our country go from a benevolent and gentle monarchy to being ruled by a tyrant, because I almost can’t remember a time now when I was proud to call my self of Vicor” Dara said and Corliss could hear the disgusted tone in her voice.

The Warden looked towards the horses as they ate, no worries towards politics or to their species in general, the only issue on there mind was simply how much food did they have. “This was not something that was instant Dara, I am sure if we wen’t back over the last decade you would find hints and plans leading up to this, the Kings death aside from convenient to her plans was a travesty and gave the Empress license to take control based on the order of succession.” Corliss stated mulling over her next statement, knowing it had been stated in back rooms and dark corners since the Emporer had married. “No one knows where the Empress came from, who her family was or how she even courted the king, there Is no documentation to her all except in the words of the Emporer dismissing the normal validation of pedigree that would usually accompany a marriage” she finished deciding not to repeat some of the rumors she had heard. But the point was valid she thought now more then ever. Who was this woman and what gave her the right to destroy the country?

Dara didn’t respond, Corliss looked over to her as the Raven-haired mage stared out to the field as well worry filled her eyes as the young girl sighed, turning to look at the Warden. “I have heard no word from the Order Corliss, I have no idea if it even still exists, some have said the order fell to the Empress’s Lord Seers and others say that the Order serves the Empress and her Seers are members of the Order, which I know is not true. But I can’t disprove the rumor either” she finished and more then fear was the frustration of an accusation against mages that was beyond damning. The last thing the Mages needed was to be associated with the demon now in power in Vicor.

Whatever happened the Mage order’s future would be tied up in the opinion of the people if they were ever able to depose the Empress, she thought still reguarding the mage. There world would take decades to recover from the mistrust and resentment she surmised but kept that to herself the mage didn’t need that on top of the burdens that had been placed on her, or the unrequited love she now experienced. Corliss thought it might be unrequited but wasn’t sure. She had seen the way Dara had protected, looked at and tried to keep close to Marcus.

The man had experienced a great loss, he tried to hide it but she could see the pain in ever motion he made, every look he gave, he had not even acknowledged Dara in a way that would invite the Mages loved, but that hadn’t stopped the woman.

It was something that would either work itself out or end up hurting the poor girl, she honestly liked her and hoped for the previous Corliss thought continuing to watch the stallions in the field.

“Dara, I have to ask, what is it with you and Marcus, I mean aside from your feelings towards him” she said a half teasing smile spreading across her face. Dara turned a bright red as she did her best to look anywhere other then directly at the Warden. “What do you mean?” she finally said her tone doing its best to seem disinterested, Corliss barked a laugh and then covered her mouth, she wasn’t trying to embarrass the poor woman she chastised herself. “I mean you obviously have feelings for him, strong feels” she continued again Dara’s shade of red deepend.

The young mage was quiet for a time and then finaly she spoke “Marcus is amazing Corliss, he is gentle and kind and risks his life to save those he doesn’t even know, despite everyting that has happened to him, his soul is pure” she explained and Corliss nodded. “Dara, he suffered a bad loss, I mean really bad, it might be a long time before he will be ready for any type of relationship” the Warden continued gently Dara just looked off into the distance “I know” she finally said and then turning to the Warden the mage continued “But he is worth the wait” Dara finished before walking towards the horses and with a shrug Corliss joined her, mounting up the two continued to ride.

The next day found them standing on a hill as the outline of the tall tower stood in the distance Corliss stood with her arms crossed studying the pillar, such an innocuous building for the rumors coming out about this place she thought. Motioning to Dara they made their way down the hill and into the heavy brush giving them cover to the complex’s wall. Slowly making their way through the thick bushes, carefully moving branches as they progressed, ensuring to minimize there noise profile, Corliss found a devent vantage point as the two looked over the eight or so guards that patrolled the courtyard as well as the other few she could count passing the windows within the building, “why the low amount of guards, didn’t the soldier say this was the place the Empress used to research magic?” Dara asked eyeing the few guards suspiciously as if at any moment they would double in count. Corliss nodded “between the borders to the east and the attack on the Northern Dominance, her soldiers are spread thin Dara, this is a damn good thing for us” Corliss said looking over the ground as well as the buildings, trying to figure out the best way to do this without dying.

Dara turned to reguard the Warden, “Please tell me you have a plan for that” she said motioning over to the courtyard with her head there was a glimmer of hope Corliss smiled “working on it” she said trying to add confidence to her words but looking at Dara she saw how well it hadn’t worked, the two women pulled back withdrawing back into the woods, Corliss, closing her eyes recounted the patrols, the guards, the tower and the other buildings, putting together a map of the facility. They needed to find a way in that wouldn’t give the soldiers the ability to execute Maelen she thought. “How do we want to do this?” Dara asked looking up at the Warden, Corliss didn’t hear her at first instead looking over towards the sky but not really seeing it Dara asked again and this time Corliss turned “We need to ensure we get in without raising the alarm, I am worried if they know we are there, Maelen will be killed” she said and Dara winced she hadn’t thought of that. “So, what do you think?” she asked again with the vision of any wrong move killing her friend.

Corliss paced for almost an hour and finally turned to the Mage “How good are you at manipulating temperature?” she asked and smiled at the now confused Mage.

Night descended upon the tower as the sun long since having disappeared behind the trees continued to fall as the waning light offered little distance to see. The guards looked sedate as they kept to there routine, most staying inside the small guard building as laughter and sometimes song spilled out as the door opened to unleash or accept another patrol. Corliss watched as, like clockwork another four guard patrol left the building and began its long circle of the property. At one time the guard house had been a storage facility for either food or goods, a squat structure the soldiers had repaired most of the walls and roof of the building, leaving it windowless with only two entrances.

Smiling the Warden ran at a crouch once the patrol had sliped out of sight around the side of the large keeps defensive wall. With a regular patrol the few guards who manned the wall bad become complacent over the months, opting to sit on the ground and chat or nap, relying on the patrol to raise the alarm, Corliss eyed the gun port that held the long resin rifle propped in it and willed the guard to stay sitting as she flitted past towards the guard house. She remained crouched taking up a good vantage point to watch the door “Come on Dara, its no or never” she whispered, looking around impatiently.

Dara stood by the small pond and using a pointed stick carved two sets of runes into the ground. She had power, nowhere near that of Maelen or Marcus but she had spent years learning how to manage what she did have. Knowing that the actions she was about to perform would tap her and badly, the Mage drew out two of the three steps into the dirt, this would allow her to simply pass the energy into it without needing to manually direct her will. Taking a breath, she began to pull energy to her, directing it towards the pond she pushed at the water willing it to heat as she poured more and more energy into it. After a short time the water began to boil as steam rose off of the surface, Dara continued to concentrate, the humidity now almost stifling as she poured even more power into the small pond. She began to feel her energy reserves ebbing and quickly turned to the first set of Runes carved into the dirt, slapping her palm against them, she suddenly felt the hot and Humid begin to cool the temperature dropping quickly as she pushed herself, pouring more power into the drawn runes. She watched as the air began to condense and fog began forming all around her. Smiling she made one last push, feeling the air significantly cool. Then with the last bit of energy, she moved her hand over to the final set of runes, the wind instantly picked up as the fog was set in motion. Dara sluggishly pulled her hand away from the last set of Runes she had carved with a simple stick and slumped to the ground, her energy escaping her and leaving the mage to do nothing but curl up on the ground and wait for her body to recover.

Still crouching by the wall, Corliss finally saw it as a wide grin spread over her face. The fog bank lazily rolled through the woods from the direction of the pond as white tendrils of fog began to caress the trees and then the field, finally coming along the outside of the wall. She felt the tendrils began to caress her skin as the cold fog drifted past her filling the courtyard. She could hear the surprise above as the guards finally noticed the strange weather, the surprise in his voice was mimicked by the second person coming to the edge of the wall. Looking up she could, for a moment see the outline of the guards until the fog thickened making it impossible to see beyond two or three feet. Corliss moved rushing towards the guard house as she hefted the large piece of wood she had been carrying since running over to the wall.

In one well practiced move Corliss slammed the bar into the two slots on the outside of the door, just as she heard something bump against the outside, the door rattled twice, and she could hear the muffled surprised voice on the other side. The soldiers weren’t getting out of there anytime soon and Corliss turned from memory pointing herself at the main building. With the soldiers now out on patrol they usually took twenty-two minutes to complete their rounds. However, with the fog she was banking on it is taking much longer, she hoped anyway. Walking forward in the thic fog she counted her steps and at the same time trying to orient herself to the fallback points she had scouted. Corliss cursed under her breath, this plan seemed a lot cleverer in her head, when she wasn’t staring down the wall of fog that now roiled in front of her. Putting her hand out she felt the cold stone wall before she saw it, the rough stone a solid reassuring pressure from the disconnected feeling she got being surrounded by the white clouds that prevented her from even seeing the ground. Closing her eyes she tried to orient herself, where was the door, she had walked from the barracks keeping to as straight a line as possible so it should be left she thought, sliding left down the wall.

She knew she had misjudged when her hand found the edge of a frame, one that came only about halfway down the stone wall, a window she thought cursing again, she must have not walked as straight as she thought, backtracking her steps along the wall until finally she felt the wood frame and tracing it down to the ground realized she had found the door. It took her only a moment to find the latch and another two to pop it using a small metal prybar, the problem with old latches is they were never very secure she thought smiling as the door opened and the thick cloud of fog fell into the room, spilling across the floor of the large room.

Corliss felt the weight of the slender pistols against her thighs, wanting to reach for them she resisted, instead pulling the two hatchets from the back of her belt, this needed to be silent she thought, until it wasn’t anymore, crouching she stepped into the room as the fog further obscured her vision. Holding her breath, she listened, reaching out with one of the only senses working and waited quietly, sound was a funny thing in thick fog she thought tilting her head as a muffled shuffling came from her left, or was it her right. Corliss strained her ears trying to find out where the sound had come from, she felt blind and disconnected, as if floating above the world in the clouds itself with the door open more fog flooded into the room, the warm air of the building fighting to dissipate it, but not fast enough it was next to impossible to see and then there, the noise came from her left. Corliss turned in time to see a shadowy figure begin to resolve in front of her as he drew close. With a practiced spin of the hatchet he brought the spear tipped end down upon the skull of the confused soldier.

Recalling the directions and layout from the soldier she used the wall as a guide, making her way deeper into the facility, she only had minutes before a guard would find the guardhouse locked or someone would raise an alarm she thought, pushing herself faster. By the time she reached the end of the long hall she nearly smashed into a wall appearing in front of her, marking the end of the hall and the turn to the basement door. Quickly finding it she flung open the door on a very surprised guard who happened to be coming up the stairs, Corliss moved jumping on the guard and landing on him knees first, he pitched down the stairs and she used his weight to come to rest standing on the steps. Taking the remaining steps two at a time she came to the bottom of the landing, turning the hatchet to the side, she used the heavy metal end to knock the guard out.

Corliss descended further down the stone spiral steps finally coming to the bottom of the dark basement. No guards met her at the landing, and she made her way down the line of cells, most were empty, some help men and women who looked up their eyes devoid of hope she noticed. Corliss tried the doors noticing the pin, she removed it allowing the doors to swing freely open. “Get out, go now” she hissed at the people who looked at her confused and then realizing that she was not a guard, they rushed for the door, some managed a quick thank you as they bolted for the stairs. Corliss kept walking down the hall to the last cell on the left. Pulling the pin, she stepped in and gasped. Hanging in the center of the room unconscious was a man, stripped half naked and shackled to the ceiling. He looked as if he had been beaten nearly to death she thought, approaching the old man slowly.

“Hello?” Corliss called and saw the man move as a groan escaped his lips and he turned his head, trying to get a look at where the voice had come from. “Easy Maelen, Marcus sent me” she said looking over the cuffs, each set had a pin and upon pulling one, his arm came free as the cuff opened. She did the same to the other one and the old man fell to the floor with a grunt. “We don’t have time for this” she said helping the old man up and throwing one of his arms over her shoulders.

It took an agonizingly long time before they reached the door to the complex again, the fog had begun to disspate making it much easier to see. Walking outside she saw the tower no longer held the sharp shooters, they must have seen the others escape and went after them she thought. Moving as fast as she could, Maelen and Corliss shuffled across the courtyard finally making it to the old wall.

A very tired looking Dara came around the corner with three horses “Maelen are you okay” she gasped coming over to the old man. “Im okay, where is Patrice?” he said his voice hoarse and tired. “She is fine” Dara said and began to help the old man onto a horse. Corliss saw the old man visibly relax, despite there current situation that one statement had set him at ease. “Stop” she heard behind them she had thought they would have more time, thought the soldiers would be more confused or take longer to regroup, but no, they were professionals and had very quickly adapted and now that the fog was quickly dissipating, the magic that fueled it now gone she turned to see the open door of the guard house and the small group of them coming towards her, swords and rifles at the ready. Corliss took a breath and then looked up at Dara as she finished mounting the horse. “Ride meet me at the camp we used last night” she said pulling the repeating rifle from the saddle holster “Go” she yelled, turning as she dropped the charging handle and heard the reassuring sound of a round entering the chamber.

Corliss spun, holding the gun at waist level and began to fire, as soon as the trigger was pulled, she would drop another round in the chamber and fire. Soldiers dropped as red blossoms appeared on there chests, after only a moment of shock, the rest dove for any cover they could find as shots wizzed past Corliss, she too was moving, firing as she went finally reaching the edge of the wall she crouched down and waited as pieces of the wall were taken off, the soldiers still firing. They are trying to keep my head down she thought as the warden could imagine a small group flanking her.

A Moment later she slung the rifle over her shoulder reaching down and pulling the slender pistols, thumbing back the hammers she spun coming around the edge of the wall and firing into the very surprised group of soldiers that had been advancing to get the drop on her. Three of the five dropped by her shots, the other two dove to either side trying to put anything between themselves and her guns.

Counting the shots, she knew when she was about to run out, without thinking she turned and bolted, jumping onto the horse she dropped down the opposite side, putting the animal in between her and the still firing soldiers. Pulling the rifle, she cocked it one handed and fired at the group as the horse galloped away, putting distance between herself and the complex.

Corliss quickly put distance between her and the guards as she rode to meet up with Dara and Maelen.
